column2: Retain Nabouchodonosor's arrival, Joakim's three-year service as slave and his turning and breaking faith. Slave represents the selected doulos in royal subordination without substituting a different political title.

Retain the unnamed he as sender, four groups of lightly equipped raiders, their dispatch into Judah to prevail and the Lord's word through prophets. The Greek does not explicitly name the Lord as the sending subject here; capitalization in He spoke refers to the subsequent divine word.
column3: Does the unexpressed initial sender continue Nabouchodonosor or imply the Lord? The reading remains unexpanded.

column2: Retain the Lord's anger, removal of Judah from His presence and Manasseh's sins. Judah is treated corporately as it, with the Lord as the contextual referent of His.

Retain the two mentions of innocent blood and the Lord's unwillingness to be propitiated. The inherited passive expression remains pending lexical review rather than being silently replaced by unwilling to forgive.
column3: Which contextual sense of hilasthenai best represents the selected divine subject and infinitive?

column2: Retain all Joakim's deeds, the presentative behold and the Judah chronicle question. Behold is grounded in the explicit source particle.
Retain Joakim for both father and son, the father's death formula and the son's succession. The repeated selected name is not silently changed to distinguish Jehoiakim from Jehoiachin.
Retain Egypt's king no longer leaving his land and Babylon's acquisition of all his territory from Egypt's torrent to the Euphrates. Again is warranted by the no-longer/add construction.
Retain age eighteen, three months in Jerusalem and Nestha daughter of Ellanathan from Jerusalem. No age or name is imported from a parallel regnal notice.
Retain evil in the Lord's eyes and everything his father had done. The singular paternal comparison remains distinct from earlier plural fathers formulas.
Retain Nabouchodonosor himself coming to Jerusalem and the city under siege. The named king is not changed to his servants from another witness.
Retain the king entering the city while his servants besieged it. The apparent chronological tension is not removed by changing entered to approached.

Retain Joakim, servants, mother, rulers and eunuchs going out and the king of Babylon taking him in the eighth year. The possessive his is contextually the Babylonian reign but is not expanded into a fresh name within the text.
Retain both temple and palace treasures and cutting apart all Solomon's gold sanctuary vessels according to the Lord's word. The destruction verb is not reduced to intact removal alone.

Retain Jerusalem, all rulers and mighty men, ten thousand captives, every craftsman and the one who shuts up, with only the poor remaining. The occupational phrase stays unresolved rather than receiving an unverified smith identification.
column3: What occupational group does the substantivized shutting participle denote here and in verse 16?

column2: Retain Joakim's deportation, mother, wives, eunuchs and the land's powerful people, with Jerusalem-to-Babylon movement. Wives remains plural and is not collapsed into a general household.

Retain seven thousand military men and one thousand craftsmen/shutting workers, described as war-capable, and repeated deportation to Babylon. The figures are not recalculated to force agreement with the ten-thousand summary.
Retain Maththanias as his son and the imposed name Sedekias. The selected son is not replaced by uncle or brother, and the possessive antecedent remains an explicit review question.
column3: Whose son does the selected pronoun identify, and how should this kinship reading be presented alongside textual evidence without replacing it?

column2: Retain age twenty-one, eleven years in Jerusalem and Amital daughter of Jeremiah. The selected shorter maternal notice contains no place of origin to supply.
Retain evil before the Lord and the comparison with Joakim. Before reflects the selected wording without introducing a fresh name distinction between the two earlier Joakims.
Retain wrath upon Jerusalem and Judah until expulsion and Sedekias's breaking faith with Babylon's king. The human rebellion follows the divine-anger account without a supplied chronology correction.
Retain ninth year, tenth month, all Nabouchodonosor's force, encampment and a surrounding siege wall. The selected verse supplies no day of the month, so none is added.
Retain the continuing siege until Sedekias's eleventh year. The duration is not converted to a calculated number of months unsupported by the omitted start day.
Retain the ninth of the month, severe famine and absence of loaves for the land's people. No fourth-month designation is imported into this selected shorter verse.

Retain the breach, all warriors' night departure through the gate between walls by the royal garden and surrounding Chaldeans. The final singular he takes the Araba road without a supplied king as explicit subject.
Retain pursuit of the king, capture in Araboth Jericho and dispersion of all his force. The two occurrences of force refer to opposing sides and are not merged.
Retain seizure, conveyance to Babylon's king at Deblatha and the singular pronouncement of judgment. The shift from plural captors to singular judging king remains.
Retain singular agency in killing the sons, blinding Sedekias, fettering him and bringing him to Babylon. The king's executive agency is not recast as an explicitly plural group of soldiers.

Retain fifth month, seventh day, nineteenth royal year and Nabouzardan as chief cook standing before Babylon's king. Chief cook reflects the inherited office rendering without claiming that its contextual military function is settled.
column3: How should archimageiros be rendered as an imperial office while retaining its Greek lexical evidence?

column2: Retain burning the Lord's house, royal house and all Jerusalem's houses, with the repeated every house clause. The final by connects to the subject in verse 10; no missing wall demolition is supplied from another witness.

Retain only the chief cook as the grammatical completion of verse 9. This brief selected unit is not expanded into the wall-destruction account of a parallel text, and its stable verse identity remains intact.

Retain the remaining city population, defectors to Babylon and remaining support as Nabouzardan's deportees. Support represents the opaque collective sterigma provisionally, not a resolved soldier or artisan category.
column3: What population is meant by the remaining support in this context?

column2: Retain some of the poor left for vineyard work and gabin. The second occupation remains transliterated pending lexical evidence, rather than silently becoming farmers.

Retain the Chaldeans as agents, bronze pillars, mechonoth and bronze sea, their breaking and the bronze's transport to Babylon. The borrowed structural term remains consistent with the inherited text.
Retain cauldrons, iamin, bowls, incense dishes and all bronze ministering utensils. The singular took is preserved without silently replacing it with the Chaldeans as a newly explicit plural subject.
column3: What object does iamin denote, and are incense dishes distinct from the next verse's firepans?

column2: Retain the chief cook's taking of firepans and gold and silver bowls. The list continues into verse 16 without claiming that all subsequent bronze objects are made of those precious metals.

Retain two pillars, one sea, mechonoth made by Solomon and the unreckoned bronze weight. The English list connection smooths the Greek nominal construction provisionally; number and material remain explicit.

Retain eighteen-cubit pillar height, three-cubit chothar, sabacha and pomegranates, all bronze, and the corresponding second pillar. Opaque architectural terms and the three-cubit figure are not replaced from earlier temple descriptions.
column3: What structural components do chothar and sabacha identify, and how does the final sabacha phrase attach?

column2: Retain Saraias as first priest, Sophonias as son of the second rank and three doorpost guards. The selected son is not omitted to create the familiar second priest title.
column3: Does son of the second order express rank idiomatically, or does the selected syntax require a different analysis?

column2: Retain one supervising eunuch, five royal-face observers, the commander's scribe mustering the people and sixty others found in the city. Five is not harmonized to another witness, and the scribe's dependency remains explicit.
Retain Nabouzardan taking the previously listed people to Babylon's king at Deblatha. The repeated transfer identifies the prisoners without adding another arrest.
Retain the king's striking and killing at Deblatha in Aimath and the summary of Judah's deportation from its own land. The selected two actions are not reduced to exile alone.
Retain the remaining population, Nabouchodonosor's leaving them and appointment of Godolias son of Achikam son of Saphan. Saphan's selected form is not silently normalized to earlier Sapphan.
Retain all commanders and men, Massephath and Ishmael, Joanan, Saraias and Jezonias with their fathers and geographical designations. The repeated they and their men remains at the close of the list.
Retain Godolias's oath, not fearing the Chaldeans' passing, settling, serving Babylon and the promised good outcome. Passing is not silently changed to servants or retaliation.
column3: Does parodos mean transit, incursion or another contextual activity in this reassurance?

column2: Retain seventh month, Ishmael's two-generation lineage, royal offspring and ten companions. The singular attacker's objects include Godolias and the Judeans/Chaldeans; the inherited parenthesis isolates Godolias's death without inventing a plural attacking verb.
column3: How far does the elliptical death statement extend beyond Godolias to the other victims?

column2: Retain all people from small to great, commanders, entry into Egypt and fear of the Chaldeans. The causal fear remains distinct from Godolias's preceding reassurance.

Retain thirty-seventh deportation year, twelfth month, twenty-seventh day, Euilmarodach's accession-year setting, lifted head and explicit prison release. The selected name Joakim remains and no differing day is substituted.
Retain kind speech and elevation of his throne above the other kings' thrones in Babylon. Kind speech renders speaking good things contextually without an added pardon formula.

Retain changed prison garments, continual eating before him and all days of life. The first he may continue the benefactor while the eater is contextually Joakim; the inherited pronouns keep the agency question visible.
column3: Should the garment-changing agent or the shift to Joakim as eater be made explicit in English after closer syntactic review?

column2: Retain continuing table provision from the royal house, each day's portion on that day and all days of his life. Continually is explicit in the source; the repeated daily and lifelong expressions are not collapsed into a generic pension.
